answer: Live CNL-0080 (the executable CNL-0059 overlay on the council stopping runtime) fires instant_unanimity_trigger on a primed round-1 unanimous council with zero independent briefs and relabels the outcome from AGREEMENT to AGREEMENT_HELD_FOR_REVALUATION. A trigger-disabled overlay-off control of the same ballots ships AGREEMENT, so the trigger is not purely ceremonial for finalization. It does not execute blind re-evaluation, forced dissent, counterexample generation, role rotation, or critic recruitment: those listed interventions are absent from the live engine. A council that reaches unanimity at round 4 after independent briefs and disagreement does not fire the trigger. Timer exhaustion and contested ballots also stay silent. question: When a council reaches unanimity in the first round with no independent briefs, does the runtime actually trigger blind re-evaluation, forced dissent, counterexample generation, role rotation or critic recruitment?

reviewer.method: Parser-free overlay-off decision tuple, not a rerun of the transcript inspection in probe 1.

title: Instant-unanimity trigger: does suspiciously fast agreement force re-evaluation?

verdicts.claim: A primed round-1 unanimous council with zero independent briefs fires CNL-0059 instant_unanimity_trigger.
Live runtime executes blind re-evaluation, forced dissent, counterexample generation, role rotation, or critic recruitment when instant unanimity is detected.
The triggered run's final decision differs from a trigger-disabled control of the same ballots (not ceremonial).
Unanimity after independent briefs and disagreement rounds does not fire the instant-unanimity trigger.
